# Sun, Earth and Moon — sources and provenance

2026-10-27. Scope: published lesson content; `sample-orbit` supplies the existing engine bindings. Source ids use the implemented `S[1-9]…` rule: S3–S9, not padded dossier ids. Retained register: **21 entries**, comprising **19 external primary bodies** and **2 Atlas original sources** (S33 calculation, S36 design). All retained external bodies were reopened for this content pass. No verbatim quotation is included.

- [S36] Atlas sun-earth-moon design study v1. DESIGN: spherical Sun/Earth/Moon with radii 695700/6371/1737.4 km, circular Earth orbit 149597870.7 km, lunar reference 384400 km and distance samples 363300/384400/405500 km (S8–S10). Fixed Earth axis 23.44°, lunar inclination 5.145°. Periods: year 31557600 s, stellar spin 86164.09054 s, lunar orbit 27.3217 × 86400 s. True scale sets Earth diameter to 10 mm; schematic display maps Earth orbit to 3.6 m, lunar reference orbit to 0.75 m, Sun radius to 0.45 m, Earth radius to 0.12 m and preserves Moon/Earth radius ratio. Experiments: coupled advances all motions; day freezes orbits and uses a DESIGN 86400 s spin; year advances only Earth orbit; moon freezes Earth orbit and spin; eclipse is a static geometric comparison; local-year selects a row from S33. / Atlas 太阳、地球、月亮设计研究 v1。设计：球形太阳、地球、月球半径分别为 695700、6371、1737.4 km，圆轨道日地距 149597870.7 km、地月参考距 384400 km，月距采样 363300、384400、405500 km（S8–S10）。固定地轴倾角 23.44°、月轨道倾角 5.145°。年周期 31557600 s、恒星自转周期 86164.09054 s、月球公转周期 27.3217 × 86400 s。真尺度取地球直径 10 mm；示意显示取地球轨道 3.6 m、月球参考轨道 0.75 m、太阳半径 0.45 m、地球半径 0.12 m，并保留月地半径比。耦合实验推进三种运动；昼夜冻结公转、设计自转周期为 86400 s；年实验只推进地球公转；月实验冻结地球公转和自转；食实验静态比较；本地年表实验只读 S33。 (SIM, not measurements, ephemerides or dated forecasts. Units kilometres, seconds and degrees; y-up ecliptic frame; one shared model time. Sun S=(0,0,0), Earth E=AU(cos λ,0,−sin λ), Moon M=E+r RY(Ω)RX(i)(cos u,0,−sin u). Earth orientation qX(ε)qY(θ) keeps its axis fixed; synchronous Moon local +X points to Earth, while disabled synchrony fixes inertial orientation. For latitude φ and solar declination δ: D=24 acos(−tan φ tan δ)/π h, clamped to 0/24 at polar limits; noon altitude=90°−|φ−δ|. These geometric-centre horizons exclude refraction; S33 independently uses −0.833°. Phase angle β is between Moon-to-Sun and Moon-to-Earth; lit fraction=(1+cos β)/2, separate from eclipse dimming. Apparent diameter=2 asin(radius/observer distance); disc separation and finite tangent cones determine eclipses at a stated model surface observer. Nominal quarter gives about 50.13%, not exactly 50%; coupled mean phase cycle=1/(1/27.3217−1/365.25)=29.5306753681 d. At 45° latitude, model daylight is about 15.43/8.57 h at opposite solstices, and 12 h at zero tilt. Earth 10 mm gives Moon about 2.73 mm, lunar centre distance 302 mm, surface gap 295 mm, Sun about 1.09 m and Earth–Sun centre distance 117.4 m. Display mappings never change physics; darkFill=0.035 is teaching fill light, not lunar brightness. No precession, N-body forces, textures, real lunar libration or atmosphere. CC0 arithmetic oracles and full equations/provenance are in data/SOURCES.md and docs/44 §§4,9. / 模拟，不是实测、星历或日期预报。km/s/deg、黄道 y 轴朝上坐标，单一模型时间。太阳 S=(0,0,0)，地球 E=AU(cos λ,0,−sin λ)，月球 M=E+r RY(Ω)RX(i)(cos u,0,−sin u)。地球姿态 qX(ε)qY(θ) 保持轴向不变；同步时月球局部 +X 朝地球，关闭同步则固定惯性朝向。纬度 φ、太阳赤纬 δ 的几何日长 D=24 acos(−tan φ tan δ)/π 小时，极区夹到 0 或 24；正午高度=90°−|φ−δ|。这是无折射的太阳中心地平线，区别于 S33 的 −0.833°。月球指向太阳与地球的夹角 β 给亮部=(1+cos β)/2，食遮暗另报。视直径=2 asin(半径/观察距离)，视盘分离与有限光源切锥决定指定模型地表点的食型。名义弦月约 50.13%，并非精确一半；耦合平均朔望周期=1/(1/27.3217−1/365.25)=29.5306753681 日。纬度 45° 的相反至点约 15.43、8.57 小时，零倾角为 12 小时。地球 10 mm 时月球约 2.73 mm、中心距 302 mm、表面间隙 295 mm，太阳约 1.09 m、日地中心距 117.4 m。显示映射不改物理；暗面 0.035 填光是教学画法，不预测月亮亮度。省略岁差、N 体、纹理、真实天平动与大气。CC0 算术对照、完整方程和出处见 data/SOURCES.md 与 docs/44 第 4、9 节。) (design study / 设计研究)

## Numerical ledger and display precision

The following are the student-facing numerical families, including quantities in PLATE, model details, controls and captions. Numeric oracle digits are internal test tolerances, not observational precision. Exact control labels such as 23.44° or 5.145° are DESIGN inputs; prose normally says about 23.4° or 5.1°. All dynamic readings are SIM; the local table is a computed estimate.

| Quantity | Origin / formula | Display and qualification |
|---|---|---|
| Mean radii Sun / Earth / Moon | S9 / S8: 695700 / 6371 / 1737.4 km | Nominal volumetric means, never substituted with equatorial radii. Diameters 1391400 / 12742 / 3474.8 km = 2r. |
| AU and nominal lunar distance | S10: exactly 149597870.7 km per AU; S8 semimajor axis 384400 km | Fixed circular model inputs, not today's measured distances. Lunar samples 363300 / 384400 / 405500 km are DESIGN; first/last are not absolute distance extrema. |
| One mean solar day / stellar spin | S10: 86400 / 86164.09054 s | Main line about 24 h / 23 h 56 min. Day experiment freezes orbit and deliberately uses a DESIGN 24 h spin. Coupled derived solar day is 86399.9949493 s, rounded about 24 h. |
| Year and lunar orbit | S10 Julian year 365.25 × 86400 = 31557600 s; S8 lunar 27.3217 × 86400 = 2360594.88 s | DESIGN circular periods. Main line about 27.32 d relative to stars and mean 29.53 d phases. Coupled mean beat period 1/(1/27.3217−1/365.25)=29.5306753681 d; never used to generate calendar dates. |
| Obliquity / lunar inclination | S9 23.44° from orbital normal; S8 5.145° to ecliptic | Main line about 23.4° / 5.1°. These are different angles. Fixed axis over a model year; no precession. |
| Latitude / orbital positions | S36 DESIGN −45°, 0°, 45°, 80°; phase/year positions are angle inputs | Axis orientation n=(0,cos ε,sin ε). Model observer longitude fixed 0°, not Singapore; table reference point is separate. 80° only illustrates polar model limits. |
| Geometric daylight / noon altitude | S36: δ=asin(n·unit(S−E)); C=−tan φ tan δ; D=24 acos(C)/π; H=90°−abs(φ−δ) | C outside ±1 clamps to 0 / 24 h. At φ45° opposite solstices: 15.4258924132 / 8.5741075868 h, main prose about 15 h 26 min / 8 h 34 min (nearest minute); zero tilt 12 h. H=68.44° / 21.56°. Solar-centre horizon; no refraction/solar-radius correction. |
| Lit fraction and phase bucket | S36: k=(1+cos β)/2; β uses Moon→Sun and Moon→Earth vectors | Nominal 90°/270° gives 50.1284773403%, displays about 50.13% or “about half”. New/full nominal points 0/100%. Eclipse dimming remains separate. Eight angle bins classify view, not precise lunar event times. |
| Finite apparent discs | S36: angular diameter=2 asin(r/d), chosen model surface observer; separation=acos(unit(O→S)·unit(O→M)) | Model Sun about 0.533°; sample lunar near/far about 0.558° / 0.499°. Observation-disc readings to three decimal degrees; declared SIM outputs and PLATE to two decimal degrees. Never fixed equal sizes; same angular ruler. No predicted contact times or true obscuration percentage. |
| Eclipse classification | S36 finite angular-disc overlap; finite-Sun tangent cones using physical radii/distances | Solar total/annular/partial/none from ordering and angular separation; lunar total/partial/penumbral/none from cone normal distances. Same-scale shadow frame; no atmosphere or red-Moon brightness forecast. |
| True scale | S36 scale factor 0.01/12742 m per km from S8–S10 | Earth 10 mm; Moon 2.727044420 mm (about 2.73 mm); lunar centre distance 301.6794852 mm (about 302 mm), surface gap 295.3159630 mm (about 295 mm). Sun 1.091979281 m (about 1.09 m); Earth–Sun centre distance 117.405329383 m (about 117.4 m). |
| Schematic scale | S36 Sun radius .45 m / Earth .12 m / Moon .12×1737.4/6371 m; Earth orbit 3.6 m / lunar reference orbit .75 m | Three distinct mappings: body radii, Earth–Sun centre distance and Earth–Moon centre distance, not one true scale. For each body radius multiplier use displayed radius / (physical radius × true factor); for each centre distance likewise. Changing scale does not change physical outputs. |
| Speeds and fill light | S36 clock rates coupled/day/year/moon = 86400/21600/2629800/196716.24 model seconds per wall second; eclipse/local-year 0; darkFill=.035 | Teaching playback speeds, not natural speeds measured on screen. Dark fill is a teaching aid. No direct mapping of grey level to real lunar surface brightness. |
| S33 dates and coordinates | Atlas DESIGN reference 1.3342°N, 103.7357°E, height 0 m; 365 days of 2026; UTC+08:00 | Not an official Observatory coordinate claim. Geometric centre crosses −0.833°, an assumed rise/set convention distinct from geometric daylight. |
| S33 day length | Original calculation S26/S33: 2026-12-21 min 722.886; 2026-06-21 max 732.005 min | About 12 h 03 min–12 h 12 min. Times nearest minute: min 07:02 / 13:03 / 19:04, max 07:01 / 13:07 / 19:13. Expanded graph axis 720–735 min. Do not replace original daylight_minutes with rounded set−rise. |
| Local event and festival date | S37: 2019-12-26 annular eclipse in Singapore; S38: lunar month 8 day 15 | Historical event evidence is separate from the undated model. No contact times, duration, path reconstruction or Gregorian festival table. S39 shows festival date need not be the exact full-Moon day. |

## Computed solar table: exact lineage

Only D03 (public numerical parameters), D04 (NOAA method) and D05 (Atlas original table) are retained from the parent dataset plan. There are no ephemerides, textures, GIS coastlines, maps or eclipse-path assets.

- Read-only source: `art/research/sun-earth-moon/singapore-sun-2026.json` in the main checkout, **90425 bytes**, SHA-256 `ab38b692020361acea7399e0bf109f13ae116192bbbdd053f90d8bfefdc8fac1`.
- Published derivative: `data/singapore-sun-2026.json`, **90248 bytes**, SHA-256 `186965767b83756043d320a4c4e8991f991d5420a76a563fa7141f90ba263a23`.
- Metadata-only changes inherited from `sample-orbit`: remove `meta.cross_check` (cut past MSS rolling-page assertion) and replace `meta.precision` with computed-estimate/minute-display/no-independent-full-year-validation wording. **All 365 daily records and summary numerical objects are identical to the source.** Coordinate, threshold, method, timezone, horizon and CC0 metadata retained.
- Reproduction check 2026-10-27: extract only pure `solar`, `root`, `hhmm` functions from source `prepare.py`; do not execute its file writes. Recompute every date using 42-step bisection of geometric altitude at −0.833°, and four iterations for equation-of-time noon. Rise/noon/set minute strings and daylight_minutes match all 365 records. This repeats the original algorithm, not independent astronomical observation.
- Source `engine-oracles.json`: **7692 bytes**, SHA-256 `cf5c121fc25fceae3b3a3b4a064cf89b21f8a7e1cd81a88b1d0c6d0ae33db54d`; original CC0 arithmetic expectations, already represented in the engine's test fixture. Not a measured ephemeris.
- NOAA method says its calculator is no longer maintained. Atmosphere, refraction and local terrain alter actual rise/set; no second-level precision, observatory scheduling or official full-year agreement is claimed.

No CC BY-SA, ODbL or ODC-BY derived asset enters this topic. CC0 table/oracle remain separate from NC-SA material (original Atlas work with no third-party licence, so the repository licence notices carry no entry for this topic). No terms acceptance, login or verification bypass was performed.

## Language and editorial limits

The exact 16 terms follow docs/44 §5: rotation, orbit, obliquity, hemisphere, daylight, solar-day, solar-noon, phase, synchronous-rotation, synodic-month, node, solar-eclipse, lunar-eclipse, annular-eclipse, apparent-diameter and lunisolar-calendar. `see` links only to other glossary ids. New/full/first/last quarter and umbra/penumbra/antumbra are explained locally without extra global terms. Chinese scientific terms are editorial choices, not MOE-certified Chinese curriculum vocabulary; HKO supports 朔望月/阴阳历, while S38 supplies local 中秋节/农历八月十五 wording.

Cut: curriculum/PSLE attribution, old MSS date validation, official observatory-coordinate and instrument-size claims, path-sampling data, blocked/index-only cultural pages and misconception-study prevalence/age claims. S38 establishes only date/wording, never an astronomical nearest/fullest-Moon explanation or universal participation.


## Content implementation notes

All 39 captions are copied verbatim from the final specification and verified
against its bilingual table by a unit test. Per-beat fact/source mapping is in
`../AUDIT.md`; numerical captions are evaluated against the actual chapter/beat
inputs, including both horizons, eclipse classification and true scale.

The actual engine uses Sun-origin frames for coupled/year and Earth-origin
frames for the other labs. Content therefore authors explicit numeric cameras
instead of registering six universal frame-inferred presets from the design
plan. Chapter 02 uses sequential Earth close views with the same inertial axis,
not a duplicate Earth or extra clock. The selectable orbital-plane guide now
contains its normal and the axial-tilt arc from that same physical snapshot.

Original PNGs remain unchanged in the read-only planned-art folder. WebP
exports use the existing illustrate.ts pipeline: cover 800/1600 px; figures
1200/2400 px (4:3). Figure @2x uses the same pipeline with a second output
variant; no new illustration, authored crop or downloaded image was added.
